title: 法巴首席经济学家：美联储还要加几次？三次可能不够
speaker: Luigi Speranza

segments.en: Rates are going up again. Fed, how many should we expect, not just today?
segments.zh: 利率又要上行了。美联储，不只是今天，我们该预期几次？

segments.en: Our base case has been for a while actually, three rate hikes. So, we expect one today, another one in December, and then January or March.
segments.zh: 我们的基准判断已经有一段时间了，是三次加息。所以我们预计今天一次，十二月一次，然后一月或三月。

segments.en: But let me put in this way, if we are wrong on three, it's because they are four, rather than two.
segments.zh: 但让我这样说，如果三次错了，那是因为是四次，而不是两次。

segments.en: I think the background is really strong. The case for rate hike is really strong.
segments.zh: 我认为背景非常强劲。加息的理由非常充分。

segments.en: We have an economy which is running about trend. We have a liberal market, which is tightening. And we have an underlying inflationary problem in the US.
segments.zh: 我们的经济大致在趋势水平运行。劳动力市场在收紧。美国还有潜在的通胀问题。

segments.en: How about its inflation problem? For us to go three, possibly four hikes. Yes. So, look, I mean, the global environment is favorable.
segments.zh: 那通胀问题呢？要让我们加三次、甚至四次。是的。你看，全球环境是有利的。

segments.en: First of all, I think that's important. Protectionism, you know, tariffs. But in general, political fragmentation is leading to what I say is, you know, subottima location of resources.
segments.zh: 首先，我认为这很重要。保护主义、关税。但总体而言，政治碎片化导致了我所说的资源次优配置。

segments.en: Then you go to the eye boost. So pressure on commodity prices, on chips, and this is showing up in the data.
segments.zh: 然后还有AI热潮。大宗商品价格、芯片价格面临压力，这在数据中有所体现。

segments.en: It was impressed by a piece of data, which is price in computers and equipment investment.
segments.zh: 有一项数据让我印象深刻，就是计算机和设备投资的价格。

segments.en: They've been in deflation for six decades, and now running in the US 11% year earlier.
segments.zh: 它们已经通缩了六十年，现在美国同比上涨11%。

segments.en: This is symptomatic of higher goods prices, which makes this underlying, quite difficult, isn't range effectively.
segments.zh: 这反映了商品价格更高，使得潜在通胀相当棘手，实际上很难控制。

segments.en: So, I would expect three would not make the trick.
segments.zh: 所以，我预计三次可能不够。

segments.en: And this is more about preventing the economy from overreacting. They're actually leading inflation to two percent within a reasonable timeframe.
segments.zh: 这更多是为了防止经济过度反应。他们实际上是在合理时间内引导通胀降至2%。

segments.en: Okay. Let me marry the Fed conversation with the long end of the Treasury curve.
segments.zh: 好的。让我把美联储的讨论与国债收益率曲线长端结合起来。
